title: Do Exponent's experts survive challenges in court?
what: When one side hires an expert witness, the other side often asks the judge to throw that expert out (a 'Daubert challenge', after a famous Supreme Court case). This chart compares how often experts get excluded in cases involving Exponent versus a baseline of similar cases without Exponent.
how: We pulled the full text of court opinions that discuss both Exponent and a Daubert/Rule 702 challenge, and had software read each one for the judge's ruling language ('motion to exclude is GRANTED' vs 'DENIED'). The same software classified a same-size set of recent non-Exponent Daubert opinions, so any classification bias hits both groups equally. Anything ambiguous is labeled 'unclassified' - never guessed.
thesis: The entire moat argument is that Exponent's 55-year courtroom-tested reputation lets it charge premium rates. If its experts survive exclusion challenges at a better-than-baseline rate, that reputation is measurably real - not marketing copy.
caveats: SMALL SAMPLE - a few dozen classifiable cases per group. Treat the comparison as indicative, not a precise statistic.
When several experts are challenged in one case, the ruling may concern a non-Exponent expert.
Every case in the list links to the actual opinion so you can read the judge's words yourself.
